title: Dependencies — patch Pydantic's moderate extra-data validation bypasses

labels.name: area:devex
labels.description: Contributor setup, development fixtures and contribution workflow.

body:
The promoted `420a9240dfb32a4192817a4c534fda474451b921` lock contains Pydantic 2.14.0 and pydantic-core 2.50.0. Both maintainer advisories below rate their validation bypass **Moderate (6.3)** and identify Pydantic **2.14.2** as fixed. PR #118 resolves that to core **2.50.2**, but also carries unrelated model/graph/database/tooling updates. Prepare a bounded Pydantic/core patch rather than requiring that complete upgrade set.

- [GHSA-qpmf-fgh3-ff25](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-qpmf-fgh3-ff25) affects Pydantic >=2.13.0,<2.14.2. It requires validating **untrusted JSON**, a model with **extra='allow'**, and an annotated **constrained extra-key type** on `__pydantic_extra__` (for example a pattern-constrained string key). JSON validation fails to validate those keys. Python-mode validation is unaffected.
- [GHSA-3r8g-cqwr-jr29](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/security/advisories/GHSA-3r8g-cqwr-jr29) affects Pydantic >=2.0,<2.14.2. It requires an **aliased TypedDict/dataclass field**, **allowed extras** (`extra='allow'` or TypedDict `extra_items`), and untrusted input containing both the alias and field name. An unvalidated extra under the field name can overwrite the validated alias value. Ordinary **BaseModel is excluded** from this second advisory because its extras are stored separately.

**Current assessment:** The source inspection found no extra-allow configuration, constrained `__pydantic_extra__` annotation, or TypedDict `extra_items` declaration establishing either prerequisite. Existing reads of `__pydantic_extra__` are not such annotations. Dependency-owned and dynamically generated schemas were not exhaustively audited. These are known affected-version findings with a patch available; no project exploit path or exploitation was demonstrated. Keep this open as a moderate security follow-up, separate from #117's critical/high work. Revisit reachability when extra handling, aliases or schema-generation paths change.

**Acceptance:**

- Inspect the exact Pydantic/core resolution and declared constraints against the existing Litestar, Pydantic AI/Graph and settings adapters; preserve their current selected versions unless a necessary edge is demonstrated.
- Check the project and relevant dependency schema paths for both exact prerequisites and record a bounded reachability disposition. Add a focused regression only for a discovered application boundary that needs it.
- Verify validation, API/schema generation and affected persistence/agent/settings boundaries, plus the repository gates required for the exact candidate. Record the commit and evidence; earlier green receipts do not transfer to changed dependency bytes.
- Requalify the maintained Scout current-authority receipt against the new Pydantic version using the actual admitted isolated OCI proof. Its freshness guard binds Pydantic alongside h11/dnspython; do not synchronize version text without new observed proof.
- Integrate through dev after the required other-human review. An automated review is not that approval.

Refs #118 and #117. This is queued maintenance; no owner or in-progress implementation claim is assigned.

## Resolution — 5 November 2026

Resolved by the accepted dependency batch in [PR #122](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/pull/122), retained on the current common main/dev commit [`7cf38797fa0d3a4204a7f38ee8d91464b449b1c6`](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/commit/7cf38797fa0d3a4204a7f38ee8d91464b449b1c6). Latest common-main [Core Python CI](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/actions/runs/41945537219) and [Repository Checks](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/actions/runs/41945537129) also passed.

The broader OCI Python gate in the repository-readiness campaign exposed seven existing rollback/foreign-restore regression failures. Core PR checks pass, but the full 3.15 run reports 12,450 passed and seven failed: [run 41781379525](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/actions/runs/41781379525), job 126413473108. This is a pre-existing boundary at `def532db`, separate from the workflow changes in #110.

The publication and Scribe settlement paths retain device/inode identifiers after releasing the object that made that identity unique. On a filesystem that promptly reuses an unlinked inode, rollback or restore can mistake a replacement object for the owned object. ADR 13 owns descriptor-relative custody and exact-object rollback.

Claimed for this campaign: retain the relevant object identity through the complete publication/restore settlement window and release every descriptor on success and failure. Scope: `file_publication_transaction.py`, `file_publication_recovery.py`, `scribe/workspace_settlement.py` and their focused existing regression modules. Preserve foreign-object refusal and all rollback outcomes; no skipped assertions, retries or timeout changes. No unrelated frontend/operator workspace changes.

Acceptance: all seven existing regressions and the two complete focused modules pass in the source-bound OCI profile; inspect descriptor cleanup across every branch, run strict lint/type checks, obtain independent review, then pass both hosted Python lanes and applicable full gates before promotion. Delivered through #110 and adopted on both long-lived branches at `420a9240dfb32a4192817a4c534fda474451b921`; the acceptance comment records the exact verification and its limits. title: Creation / Orb: show exact Run-linked investigation metadata
body:
Claim a bounded Creation evidence summary inside the existing selected-Run Orb view. A terminal Run can coexist with incomplete Creation custody; the operator needs the exact retained relationship and separate judgments without opening private bodies or inferring success from DONE. This is a read-only projection, not a new instrument or Creation action. Parent work remains [#89](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/issues/89) and [#40](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/issues/40).

The existing owners are [ADR 15: projection and retained Orb SSE](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/15-frontend.md#snapshots-streams-and-recovery), [ADR 16: separate native, external and owner judgments](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/16-sdlc.md#retain-external-assessment-before-another-change), and the [Creation current-local-authority contract](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/compositions/creation/index.md#current-local-authority). Preserve those owners before implementation and synchronize their delivery evidence before adoption.

Acceptance:

- Resolve the exact selected Run only through its retained unique Creation admission-to-case link. Unknown, unlinked, mismatched, unavailable or disabled-composition cases expose no summary; workflow names and Session proximity are not substitutes for identity.
- Enforce actual current local-operator credential possession, required scopes and Creation read policy before and after persistence reads and at every SSE poll. Revoked or reconstructed markers grant no access. Fresh current-role historical reading does not require a warm model or renewed execution authority.
- Use a dedicated bounded SELECT projection. Reading must not expire, settle, repair, lock for mutation, release or renew custody, even with an expired deadline and an encumbered slot. Compare all retained custody rows before and after the database read.
- Serve only bounded case/admission/Run identities, retained status and reason codes, deadline/slot metadata, constructor/verifier presence and adoption, candidate/verdict presence, and native/external/owner disposition metadata. Exclude source bytes, prompts, response/candidate/report bodies, free-text reasons, principals, authentication generations and credentials.
- Label native verdict, latest external assessment and owner disposition separately. Show absent, incomplete and stale state explicitly. A Run terminal status or native accepted verdict must not imply semantic correctness, external agreement or owner permission.
- Carry authorized typed metadata through the existing snapshot and evidence SSE. Metadata changes may retain the ledger cursor; recheck authority while polling. Preserve bounded streams, gaps and teardown. Once terminal evidence drains and settled closes the stream, later feedback requires an authoritative reload unless a separate live contract is proven; do not imply continued observation or complete history. Fence late responses when the selected Run or account changes.
- Keep the existing Orb inspector accessible with semantic labels, keyboard operation and non-color distinctions. Generate transport/client contracts from the server boundary; the browser receives no Composition policy or private custody objects.
- Verify exact-link/nonmutation/current-authority database controls; optional-composition, leak and SSE cases; affected generated contracts, frontend checks/build and tests; independent review, repository gates and owning State/documentation synchronization. Browser acceptance is claimed only after actual observation.

- Run existing coordinator repeated-cancellation coverage separately; do not attribute shielding or process recovery to store-only tests.
- Run the focused and full PostgreSQL module, affected unit tests and required repository gates; update State of Work only to the evidenced boundary.

---

Implement one admitted Scout Search through a pinned SearXNG service, returning attributed locators and snippets without fetching results.

**Starting point:** Search remains Designed. The native single-page Fetch/Extract workflow is now Partial under #43; it does not activate Search. The [reviewed Search contract](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/59549ab/docs/adr/30-webcrawler.md#searxng-search-contract) defines one qualified engine, one page and at most ten observations. This is separate from static Fetch/Extract (#43) and multi-page Crawl (#51).

## First working slice

- [ ] Add the Scout-owned, registrant-bound, sealed provider contribution and exact execution binding, reusing #68/#42 interface/profile/driver ownership. Expose only the effect-scoped Scout tool.
- [ ] Qualify an immutable SearXNG image, effective engine configuration and dialect. Fix query/response limits, finite contact plan, service resources and deadlines. Refuse query routing syntax, redirects, extra parameters and unsupported filters.
- [ ] Implement cooperative engine-request mediation with independently denied direct egress. Every engine/auxiliary transmission needs ADR 09's exact target, final bytes, influence/disclosure basis and budget decision before transmission. A container and engine allowlist alone are insufficient.
- [ ] Prove no hidden retry or fallback, including the connection-error branch in reviewed upstream revision ad46ebd7d. Cancellation and uncertain crash outcomes preserve attempt identity and prevent blind replay.
- [ ] Normalize attributed observations, declared losses and partial/unknown coverage. Distinguish empty results from failures; host authority/egress or adapter-transport failure cannot become successful partial results.
- [ ] Verify privacy, mediation bypass, binding drift, engine failure, malformed/oversized returns, injection and crash/cancellation against the ADR acceptance matrix; update State only to the proved boundary.

**Connections:** #38 general privacy/egress, #68/#42 capabilities, #36 safe observation, #43 page acquisition, #23 durable custody and #30 separate memory admission/promotion.

**Non-goals:** rendering, crawling, paid fallback, generated answers, automatic page contact, retention or memory promotion.

**Open qualification:** No compliant upstream mediation hook, engine profile or image is established. Find the smallest auditable integration seam without vendoring the engine catalogue or transparent TLS interception.

**Design evidence:** [59549ab](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/commit/59549ab). Documentation gates do not prove live acquisition.


### Pinned transport and engine findings — 18 October 2026

[Main `3bf598d9`](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/commit/3bf598d9189831994d4c057927b2588ed53127e0) publishes the [current source study](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/3bf598d9189831994d4c057927b2588ed53127e0/docs/sepulcher/extensions/scout-web-research.md#searxng-transport-cut) and [dated offline observation](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/3bf598d9189831994d4c057927b2588ed53127e0/tests/fixtures/scout/searxng-transport-cut-2026-10-18.json). At exact SearXNG revision `1c10abe2d3e4ab7ddcc4e9da1a7d07dc7ca7f8f4`, the unmodified `Network.call_client` method makes two controlled client/request calls after a first connection error even with `retries=0`. Four actual extracted-method offline cases pass; these are controlled collaborators, not curl transport or provider evidence.

A separate private AGPL service candidate replaces the retrying path before client acquisition and closes `get_client` itself. Six actual patched-method/real-hook cases pass: absent context, streaming refusal, one-use success, terminal failure, consumption before suspension/cancellation, and direct-client refusal. Independent static review found no P1/P2 within that narrow scope. The patch stays outside Core; no full upstream module, service, image, authenticated channel or containment boundary was executed or qualified.

Pinned engine inspection also changes the first-profile choice. Mojeek's uncached request obtains a CAPTCHA-derived cookie through auxiliary challenge/verification contacts. No challenge was executed. DuckDuckGo HTML is only a candidate: first page uses POST; CAPTCHA raises, while HTTP 303 returns empty results. A trusted bridge must refuse a redirect before that parser, and guard optional cookies and query-bearing diagnostics. No engine query or parser qualification occurred.

Required next boundary: a finite bidirectional channel from a network-denied worker to trusted host transport, with one host-authored exact-byte request, bounded response and independently observed direct-egress refusal. A synthetic isolated HTTPS proof may establish that prerequisite only. Production Search still needs its own current authority/preparation/disclosure reservation, pinned query dialect and engine/response profile, authenticated service ingress and complete lifecycle/accounting. Existing page/RSS `FETCH` authority cannot authorize Search.

Validation: 35 architecture tests passed, clean documentation passed, 644 local targets and 51 published fragments checked, including the preserved old feed-experiment anchor. [Exact-head Core CI](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/actions/runs/39112193297) and [documentation build/deployment](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/actions/runs/39112193313) pass. Only three study/State/observation files changed; production source is unchanged. All implementation checkboxes and this issue remain OPEN.

## Purpose and boundary

Map the Dispatcher surface from typed capability demand to one exact eligible grant, and route each bounded delivery slice without turning dispatch into lifecycle orchestration or workflow ownership.

[ADR 22 — Dispatcher](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/22-dispatcher.md) owns accepted dispatch law. [ADR 23 — Orchestrator](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/23-orchestrator.md) owns physical convergence. This issue is a decomposition and evidence map, not another runtime component.

## Child-issue register

- [ ] #7 — first capability selection, exact WARM grant, and lease path
- [ ] #17 — configurable ranking and bounded fallback among already eligible candidates

## Related constraints and consumers

- #16 owns resource policy and admission inputs.
- #42 proves one typed non-model capability without creating a parallel dispatcher.
- #8 consumes grants from Graph execution and must park handle-free when readiness requires convergence.
- #22 owns durable service attempts and worker recovery.
- #62 reviews the advanced composition of concurrent Intents and execution roads; it does not own Dispatcher implementation.

## Required decision sequence

```text
typed demand + pinned policy
→ enumerate declared candidates
→ reject semantic / authority / evidence / readiness ineligibility
→ rank only the eligible set
→ issue one exact WARM grant and lease
   or return a typed refusal / wait-for-convergence result
→ after convergence or changed evidence, redispatch from fresh truth
```

## Laws to preserve

- Eligibility is a hard gate; scoring never rescues an ineligible candidate.
- Provider identity, capability interface, semantic compatibility, readiness, and authority remain distinct.
- Dispatcher selects and grants; it never starts, stops, drains, or mutates a managed capability.
- A cold-but-admissible capability produces a wait/converge/redispatch cycle, not a silent semantic fallback.
- Fallback is limited to declared, semantically compatible alternatives and a total retry/effect budget.
- Possible submitted effects reconcile under their original identity; they are not blindly reissued through another road.
- Decisions pin policy generation and evidence provenance sufficient for replay, audit, and honest refusal.
- Leases are bounded, fenced, and released before a Run parks for work it awaits.

## Completion condition

Close this master when the first grant path and bounded ranking/fallback path have executable evidence; every eligibility and readiness row has deterministic behavior; redispatch after convergence uses fresh evidence; and the remaining advanced policies are separately owned or explicitly deferred.

Closure means dispatch law and delivery routes are coherent. It does not claim general scheduling, fleet placement, or arbitrary workflow orchestration.

Define and rehearse the missing lifecycle between “one local shim registers” and “an extension-bearing Vessel generation is safely installable, migratable and recoverable.”

This is a bounded child of #63. It does not turn #21 registration into a package manager, let extensions run arbitrary Alembic code at import time, or replace the owners in #45 Packaging, #46 Evolution and #47 Persistence.

**Starting point:** [ADR 05](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/05-extensions.md) accepts built-in and private coupled paths while deferring the independent package API; [ADR 17](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/17-packaging.md) requires source-bound packaging; [ADR 18](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/18-evolution.md) requires an inactive candidate and a new Vessel generation. Current #21 explicitly defers dependency locks, upgrades and migrations.

## First working slice

Choose one exact built-in or private coupled extension with a real typed contribution and, if the chosen slice needs persistence, one owned schema change. Then:

- [ ] Bind Core revision, extension source revision, activation id, contribution identities, Python/system dependency inputs, relevant locks, platform/base-image inputs and verification plan in one candidate manifest.
- [ ] Resolve and build the complete selected body before activation. Detect dependency conflicts, missing inputs, incompatible Core coupling and a changed base before any live mutation.
- [ ] Declare extension-owned persistent models separately from registration. Pin the migration lineage/head, ordering dependencies, data owner, runtime-versus-migration credentials and supported source schema.
- [ ] Rehearse a fresh install and one supported previous generation on a disposable database with retained rows. Refuse revision collisions, missing dependencies, multiple heads without an admitted merge, and an extension migration that is absent from the selected manifest.
- [ ] Verify enable → new generation → contribution/data visible, and disable → new generation → executable contribution absent while retained data follows explicit policy. Disable must not silently drop tables, delete artifacts or unload code from a live Vessel.
- [ ] Exercise one failed install/migration/activation. Record whether the declared recovery is rollback, forward repair or containment; do not report a generic “uninstall succeeded” while schema or external effects remain.
- [ ] Bind the resulting package/archive/image identities into #45 evidence and use #46 for the changed-body activation/recovery rehearsal.
- [ ] Document the minimal extension-author journey and conformance checks without promising the deferred independent SDK.

## Contract split

| Concern | Owner / coordination |
| --- | --- |
| Contribution kinds, provenance, registration seal and compatibility tier | ADR 05, #63 |
| Settings/Rune selection and immutable generation | ADR 12, #64, #1/#21 |
| Core and extension schema ownership, transactions and credential separation | ADR 06, #47 |
| Source/dependency/platform locks and artifacts | ADR 17, #45 |
| Candidate compatibility, quiescence, new process generation and recovery | ADR 18, #46 |
| Whole-installation capture/restore | ADR 07, #44 |
| Feature-specific table meaning, retention and destructive deletion | The receiving Core office or Extension Domain; never this generic lifecycle issue |

## Open decision

Select the first exact extension and determine whether its accepted slice genuinely needs a database migration. If it does, agree the manifest representation and Alembic lineage/ordering contract under ADRs 05/06/17/18 before implementation. Do not invent a dummy migration merely to satisfy this issue.

## Later

A stable independent extension API/SDK, remote package discovery, public registry, signature policy, multi-party publication and arbitrary cross-language in-process ABI remain deferred. They require their own accepted contracts and cannot be inferred from a successful private coupled rehearsal.

**Verification:** isolated build environment; disposable PostgreSQL fresh/upgrade/failure fixtures when applicable; process-generation restart; artifact and recovery receipts. Shared contribution and touched-docs rules: #52.

> **Planning representation replaced — 6 November 2026.** The contribution/decomposition route continues in #52, with named future outcomes in #62. This closure does **not** mean the capability is complete or cancelled. The original scope and evidence below remain preserved; current selected work starts at #52.

---

> **Scope split with Extension Master #63:** this issue is the map of operator-selectable and tunable values—principally global Settings, Rune schemas/instances, exact registered references, bounded policy and their immutable generations. It does **not** define how Backend, Altar, Graph, Animator/Connector, Composition or Packaging become extensible. Those contribution surfaces and their child issues belong to #63; this master specifies how an already admitted surface may be configured without turning data into code or authority.


Map everything LychD may configure, the source and scope of each value, and the boundary between declared intent, runtime observation, durable truth and authority. This is a **tracking and decomposition issue**, not a second configuration implementation.

Canonical law remains in [ADR 12 — Configuration](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/12-configuration.md). Supporting owners include [ADR 05 — Extensions](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/05-extensions.md), [ADR 08 — Containers](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/08-containers.md), [ADR 09 — Security](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/09-security.md), [ADR 22 — Dispatcher](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/22-dispatcher.md), [ADR 23 — Orchestrator](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/23-orchestrator.md) and [ADR 28 — Workflow](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/28-workflow.md). Issues cite these decisions; ADRs do not embed the mutable backlog.

## Configuration surface map

| Surface | Scope / representation | Delivery / bounded work | Boundary to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Global Settings | One immutable `lychd.toml` generation plus declared environment/file-secret precedence | #1 | Closed typed root; unknown/obsolete fields fail; every accepted field has a real consumer |
| Rune instances | Typed TOML leaves in owned anchors with path identity and provenance | #1, #21 | Runes declare intent; they are not runtime objects, registries, raw units or authority |
| Extension selection | Exact built-in/Crypt activation ids | #21 | Selection permits one boot registration generation; it does not start services or enable arbitrary neighbours |
| Host realization | Validated generation compiled into owned deployment plans | #3, #18 | Revalidate ports, secrets, mounts, routes and ownership before effects; direct raw unit injection is forbidden |
| Capability instances and profiles | Exact registered interface/profile/driver refs plus bounded overlays | #42 | Configuration cannot invent capabilities, proved limits, permissions or provider readiness |
| Dispatch ranking and fallback | Versioned bounded policy over already eligible candidates | #17 | Eligibility and authority remain hard constraints; fallback cannot silently change semantic road |
| Delegated runtime selection | Exact `[weaver.delegation]` revision/runtime/profile for new Runs | #28; retained `delegated_rite@2` selection delivered | Retained intent/checkpoints cannot be redirected by newer Settings; registration supplies no execution or egress authority |
| Resource and lifecycle policy | Declared limits, service classes and transition policy | #16, #50 | Measurements and current readiness are observations, not TOML truth; Orchestrator owns physical convergence |
| Scroll/casting selection | Exact registered Scroll, implementation, Agent/Posture and Context refs plus bounded policy | #29 | Canonical Scroll remains typed JSON; no Python imports, Graph nodes, arbitrary prompts, source bytes, credentials or live handles |
| Application/Gateway deployment profiles | One exact registered profile revision and role set | #3, #57, later Composition-specific work | Loose booleans cannot assemble partial authority, migration, network or credential topology |
| Altar editing | Typed staged request, whole-tree validation and explicit apply/reload | #56 | UI does not gain ambient filesystem, secret, activation or promotion authority |
| Presentation preferences | Finite validated semantic fields when admitted | #56 or a later bounded frontend slice | No raw CSS/selector or extension side channel; accessibility invariants remain frontend-owned |
| Secrets | References in Codex; values resolved once through the accepted secret boundary | #1, #37 | Secret values never enter TOML, snapshots, ordinary telemetry or generated samples |

## Generation and change requirements

- [ ] State the owner, source, scope, units, defaults, bounds and precedence for every configurable value.
- [ ] Distinguish global Settings, reusable profile defaults, Rune-local overlays, request-time overrides and observed runtime facts.
- [ ] Validate the complete selected Settings/extension/Rune generation before reconciliation; downstream consumers never reopen the files.
- [ ] Pin admission-relevant selection for existing Runs. A newer configuration generation affects only lawfully new admissions unless an owning migration says otherwise.
- [ ] State whether a change is a no-op reconciliation, explicit reload, service restart, new Vessel generation or typed Evolution effect.
- [ ] Missing, stale, contradictory and unsupported values fail visibly; they never trigger a hidden default provider, route or authority.
- [ ] Configuration chooses only already registered and authorized identities. It cannot register code, create Graph edges, grant effects, prove readiness or rewrite durable history.
- [ ] Samples and editor projections remain inactive or staged until explicitly applied and revalidated.
- [ ] State of Work and maintained receipts distinguish typed validation from live host/model/network acceptance.

## Existing first slices

- #1 owns the delivered Settings/Rune loader and editable-sample journey.
- #21 owns extension selection plus one contributed Rune schema.
- #3 owns compilation and reconciliation into host topology.
- #16/#17 own resource policy and bounded ranking/fallback.
- #29 owns the first exact Scroll/casting selection boundary.
- #42 owns one typed non-model capability instance.
- #56 owns one validated Altar edit/save path.
- #63 owns the complete contribution/lifecycle map rather than expanding Configuration into package management.

## Completion dimensions

Treat closure as two independent proofs:

1. **Map completeness:** every admitted field, selector, precedence edge, and generation transition has one owner and a bounded route or explicit deferral.
2. **Operator journey evidence:** one maintained edit → preview/diff → validate → apply → reload/restart path proves immutable generation handling, error visibility, secret boundaries, and effect ownership.

A complete field map does not prove the journey; one working editor does not make every value safely configurable.

## Completion condition

Close this master when every admitted field and future selector in ADR 12 has a bounded issue or explicit deferral; cross-surface precedence and generation transitions are unambiguous; and one maintained operator route shows edit/preview/apply/restart behavior without leaking authority.

Closure means the configuration map and decomposition are coherent. It does not mean every Designed selector or UI editor has shipped.

> **Planning representation replaced — 6 November 2026.** The contribution/decomposition route continues in #52, with named future outcomes in #62. This closure does **not** mean the capability is complete or cancelled. The original scope and evidence below remain preserved; current selected work starts at #52.

---

Track **every supported way LychD can grow** and route each extensibility surface to one bounded child issue or an explicit closed/deferred decision. This is the parent map; it is not a second architecture source and not one implementation assignment.

Canonical law remains in [ADR 05 — Extensions](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/05-extensions.md). Each receiving office keeps its own authority: Backend, Frontend, Configuration, Persistence, Workers, Graph/Workflow, Packaging, Evolution, Security and the relevant Extension Domain. Issues cite those decisions; ADRs do not embed the mutable backlog.

## What this master means by an extension surface

An **extension surface** is a shaped contract through which an explicitly selected package may contribute a versioned thing to one receiving owner. It is broader than the current five-store boot context and narrower than arbitrary plug-in code.

Keep these distinct:

```text
package/source admission
→ explicit selection
→ typed contribution registration
→ configuration of exact admitted identities
→ runtime/application activation
→ host-owned backend and Altar projection
→ packaging, restart/evolution and recovery
```

Configuration Master #64 primarily maps Settings, Runes, exact selectors and bounded policy **after an extensibility surface exists**. It does not define how Backend, Altar, Graph, Animator, Composition or Packaging become extensible.

## Child-issue register

- [x] #21 — first explicitly selected local package, shaped Contribution and Rune schema
- [ ] #65 — package manifest, dependency/system locks, migrations, install/upgrade/disable and recovery
- [ ] #66 — backend service/operation and host-owned HTTP projection
- [ ] #67 — Altar projection through closed descriptors and Core-owned rendering
- [ ] #68 — Animator, Connector, interface/profile/driver/activation and end-to-end capability call
- [ ] #29 — Spell implementation, Scroll publication, immutable resolution and Graph binding
- [ ] #69 — Composition revision, Pattern catalogue, deployment/application profile and projections

Parallel master: #64 owns configurable/runic objects, precedence and immutable configuration generations.

## Extensibility surface map

| Surface that must be extendable | Admitted mechanism | Owning / bounded issues | Boundary and current status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Package source, Python/system dependencies, binaries, images and licences | Forge/candidate manifest with exact source, locks, platform inputs, legal inventory and receipts | #65, #45 | Designed lifecycle; a running Vessel never installs its own trusted dependencies |
| Package selection and boot registration | Exact built-in/Crypt activation id and one sealed assembly pass | #21 | Partial foundation exists; installed is not active and there is no scanning or live unload |
| Settings, Rune schemas and Rune instances | Shaped schema contribution plus immutable typed configuration generation | #1, #21, master #64 | Configuration selects admitted identities; it does not import code, start runtimes or grant authority |
| Backend services and operations | Owner-qualified service/operation contribution adapted by the Vessel composition root | #66 | Designed; no arbitrary Litestar controller, middleware or route-bundle mutation |
| HTTP/API projection | Host-owned versioned DTO/controller over an admitted backend contract | #66 | Designed; route, auth, errors, OpenAPI and collisions remain Backend-owned |
| Persistent models and migrations | Explicit schema owner, manifest-pinned Alembic lineage/order, separate migration credentials and recovery policy | #47, #65 | Registration never implies table or migration authority |
| Durable jobs, workers and service attempts | Typed job/attempt contribution using ordinary Workers recovery and settlement | #22, #66 | No extension-owned scheduler, queue law or second recovery ledger |
| Animator and Connector providers | Separate interface, profile, dialect driver, activation, Rune and evidence contributions | #68, #42, #55 | Designed general surface; provider identity, semantic compatibility and readiness remain distinct |
| Soulstone/local runtime and Portal/remote runtime definitions | Typed Animator definition and lifecycle-specific adapter | #5, #6, #21, #55, #68 | Local lifecycle and remote custody remain different; registration starts neither |
| Agent and delegated-runtime adapters | Exact Agent builder or bounded delegated runtime declaration/adapter | #5, #28 | Adapter receives only its declared containment; it is not a Graph or authority kernel |
| Spell contracts and implementations | Separate shaped contract and executable implementation stores | #29 | Designed public catalogue; registration of contract, implementation and activation are separate |
| Scrolls, Patterns and Graph binding | Versioned restricted Scroll plus exact adapter and Resolution Lock | #29; execution #8 and advanced topology #61 | Extend Graph by admitted score/adapter, **not** by live node/edge mutation or package scanning |
| Graph topology capabilities | Versioned adapter support for admitted serial, subgraph, branch and join grammar | #8, #61 | Topology support is Graph-owned; an extension may publish only scores the admitted adapter can prove |
| Composition/application contracts | Owner-qualified immutable Composition revision with records, judgment, effects, projections, outcomes and recovery | #69 | Designed runtime contribution; documentation Portfolio membership alone is not registration or delivery |
| Product, Suite and deployment selection | Exact revision/profile selection over already admitted Composition/Suite contracts | #69, #29, #3 | Product packaging cannot manufacture missing application truth or authority |
| Altar visibility and interaction | Closed versioned projection/descriptor rendered by Core-owned Svelte instruments | #67, #14, #56 | Designed; no extension-owned HTML, JavaScript, Svelte, arbitrary CSS, imports or runtime routes |
| Palette and interface locale packages | Finite semantic palette map or static message catalogue with accessibility/licence receipts | #67, #45 | Explicitly deferred bounded data contribution, never a CSS/component plug-in API |
| Artifact and storage providers | Typed ArtifactRef/custody adapter under the owning storage contract | #23 | Provider cannot infer adoption, promotion or application meaning |
| Domain effects and providers | Separate effect-specific contribution accepted by the receiving Domain | A2A #19, Toll #32, Scout #43/#51, Echo #48, Vision #49 and their owning issues | Capability registration grants no network, payment, crawl, media or declassification authority |
| Deployment service roles and host topology | Versioned deployment-service contribution compiled into an owned manifest | #3, #18, #65 | Cannot inject undeclared commands, ports, mounts, networks, secrets, migrations or dependencies |
| CLI/operator operations | Inert typed operation metadata beneath one future host-owned namespace | #2 | Root grammar and extension Click callbacks remain closed; dynamic operation catalogue is deferred |
| Evidence and inspection | Typed producer-attributed events/projections consumed by Oculus/Altar | #36, #67 | Observation has no registration, execution, promotion or effect authority |
| Assimilation and promotion of foreign craft | Candidate → review/evaluation → source-bound package → Evolution | #35, #40, #45, #46, #65 | Candidate material is not an active extension until every admission and recovery gate passes |
| Independent public extension SDK/registry | Versioned public API, conformance suite, signed publication and Forge distribution | future bounded work after coupled path | Explicitly deferred; current built-in/private coupling creates no compatibility promise |

## Reference vertical: one extension across the whole body

The child issues should eventually prove one coherent author journey rather than unrelated toy registries:

1. Bind the package source, dependencies, platform and licences (#65/#45).
2. Select it explicitly and register exact contributions plus Rune schemas (#21/#64).
3. Add one Animator/Connector capability if needed (#68/#42), with effects owned by its Domain.
4. Add its backend service, optional durable worker and explicitly owned persistence (#66/#22/#47/#65).
5. Publish one Spell/Scroll and, where justified, one Composition/application profile (#29/#69).
6. Expose a host-owned API and safe Altar projection (#66/#67).
7. Build an inactive candidate, restart into a new Vessel generation, verify, disable/upgrade and recover (#45/#46/#65).

No step implies the next. The end-to-end receipt must preserve identity and provenance across all of them.

## Cross-cutting requirements

- [ ] Every Contribution declares receiving owner, kind, stable identity, immutable revision/digest, Registrant provenance and any separate concrete Provider.
- [ ] Package admission, selection, registration, configuration, activation, effect authority, application publication, projection and promotion remain separate decisions.
- [ ] Cross-store references validate as one staged generation before membership seals; runtime code cannot mutate the registry.
- [ ] Executable code, dependency, selected-package or contribution-contract changes enter through a new Vessel generation.
- [ ] Each surface states collision, compatibility, disable/retention, migration, recovery and evidence behavior.
- [ ] Extensions use ordinary backend, worker, Graph, security, persistence and frontend laws; they do not create parallel kernels or authority ledgers.
- [ ] Deliberately closed surfaces are named as closed. “Extensible” never means arbitrary callbacks, imports, routes, UI code, Graph mutation or host commands.
- [ ] Evidence distinguishes unit registration, disposable migration, clean-host packaging, process restart, named-host operation and recovery.

## Completion dimensions

Treat closure as two independent proofs:

1. **Map completeness:** every listed surface has one canonical owner and a bounded delivered, planned, or explicitly deferred route.
2. **Vertical evidence:** one admitted reference extension crosses source/dependency binding, selection, typed contribution, configuration, backend/worker/persistence where applicable, Spell/Scroll or Composition binding, safe Altar/API projection, restart/upgrade/disable, and recovery.

A complete map does not prove the vertical; one successful vertical does not prove every surface is owned.

## Completion condition

Close this master when every row has a canonical owner and a delivered, bounded or explicitly deferred child route; one reference extension traverses the complete admitted vertical with retained evidence; and the author guide makes clear which surfaces are open, descriptor-driven, owner-adapted or deliberately closed.

Closure means the extensibility map and decomposition are coherent. It does not mean every future surface or independent SDK has shipped.

## Delivery review — 12 October 2026

Published source: [a913bff](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/commit/a913bff9d544b84abc14f9589bbfc59ec52f3e98).

Built-in activation contributions use dependency-first registration, registrant attribution and sealed owned stores; fresh-process tests cover selected/disabled extensions and retained configuration. The new private legacy-inline binding preserves v2 public snapshots and adds no portable public extension protocol. Package lifecycle, backend/Altar contributions and the complete independently owned reference extension journey remain open in the existing child issues.

The bounded registration/configuration/restart slice in #21 is now completed with the Phoenix authoring example, ownership/admission checks and fresh-interpreter enable/configure/disable evidence. Its closure does not complete the full reference vertical or the general interface/profile/driver extension contract. Remaining child issues and cross-cutting checks stay open.

[Delivery evidence](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/a913bff9d544b84abc14f9589bbfc59ec52f3e98/docs/state-of-the-work.md#extension-activation-contributions) · [Core CI](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/actions/runs/38225082480)

<!-- lychd-critical-review-2026-10-14 -->
## Complexity disposition — 14 October 2026

Review base: [`58bbd720`](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/commit/58bbd7206d8cec61c228cda32ef33f6babed0a66). Retain the implemented five shaped stores, registrant attribution, explicit selection and sealed process generation. Fresh-interpreter and mocked Crypt→Dispatcher→Nexus evidence give this machinery a concrete purpose; it is not an unbounded plugin kernel.

The first useful improvement application can be an explicitly owned source Pattern using existing runtime and Archive seams. General Pattern/evaluator contribution stores, dynamic imports and a public SDK are not prerequisites. The existing coupled consumer is already demonstrated. Reopen an independent SDK/compatibility promise only for independently versioned downstream consumers with concrete compatibility and upgrade requirements.

Before claiming changed-body continuation or automated extension promotion, prove exact code/config/model closure identity and reject a changed closure under reused labels (#29/#65/#46). Capability-key pinning and the boot-local `module:qualname` inline binding do not provide that portable proof.

Sequence #33's small comparison and #40/#35's inert candidate before #46's controlled replacement rehearsal. Keep hot reload, automatic installers and future distributed quorum/roster machinery deferred for first light. This changes delivery priority, not ADR ownership or the remaining child acceptance criteria.

> **Planning representation replaced — 6 November 2026.** The accepted **Measured runtime policy and advanced execution** outcome is retained in #62. Reopen one bounded task when selected. This closure does **not** mean the capability is complete or cancelled. The original scope and evidence below remain preserved; current selected work starts at #52.

---

Add nested subgraphs and bounded parallel branches after the local multimodal and runtime-policy paths are proven. The current Graph adapter is serial; this is an advanced follow-up.

## Checklist

- [ ] Admit one versioned topology under ADR 24: isolated typed branch state, parent/child identities, bounded fan-out and explicit join/reduction. A waiting branch allows independent siblings to continue.
- [ ] Reuse the capability handshake per branch: Dispatcher selects; Orchestrator starts the Animator and/or activates its model; resume dispatches afresh. Cover a running llama.cpp router with an unloaded or already-loading target, without duplicate loads or inference-triggered autoload.
- [ ] Resolve only branches and router alternatives declared by the pinned Scroll. Admission may fold those alternatives into one typed execution projection using exact predicates and capability evidence; it must not generate edges or rewrite the live Graph. A missing/cold capability yields the declared wait, refusal or bounded same-road fallback, never an undeclared semantic branch.
- [ ] Integrate #16's resource policy and #17's configurable ranking/fallback. Waiting branches hold no grants; competing branches preserve drain/ownership rules and have bounded wait/retry budgets instead of unbounded model switching.
- [ ] Define parent/child deadline, cancellation and failure propagation; settle every started branch. Checkpoint branch/join progress and recover only admitted boundaries using #22's service-attempt contract; never serialize live handles or blindly replay uncertain effects.
- [ ] Demonstrate one nested two-branch workflow and two competing Runs, including one cold capability, one independent warm branch, a join and cancellation. Retain deterministic/recovery fixtures plus a named-host receipt correlated through #36.

**Completion dependencies:** #16, #17 and #22. These already lead back to #8 and the earlier runtime/multimodal foundations. Contract proposals and fixtures may start earlier; this work does not block those foundations.

**Open decision:** Agree the first subgraph/branch checkpoint schema and join/cancellation semantics before implementation. Preserve #21's extension registration and #1's typed configuration boundaries.

The default is read-only. Explicit `CANVAS_AUTHORING=1` admits only Canvas and Project authoring into disposable memory under normal security checks; execution, consent and physical transitions remain refused. ## Task-based acceptance from review — 14 October 2026

Review base: [`58bbd720`](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/commit/58bbd7206d8cec61c228cda32ef33f6babed0a66). The read-only synthetic fixture is a useful contributor boundary; retain it and qualify these concrete tasks:

- Following published commands, authenticate with terminal-issued credentials, identify the sample as synthetic, follow its exact Run Bridge→Orb→Loom→back using only the keyboard, with visible focus and retained selection.
- Repeat incorrect credentials, backend unavailable, and fixture restart; distinguish expired ephemeral credentials from an executing Run failure. Show the refusal of mutation without suggesting a model ran.
- On the separately admitted executing browser path (#11), preserve a later draft and original request identity across lost admission acknowledgment and navigation. Inspect consent/unknown/cancel outcomes without duplicate submission.
- Include long identifiers, narrow view, 400% zoom and reduced motion; ask the operator what happened, what is unknown, whether retry is safe and what another turn will remember.

The 14 October offline review reran developer-fixture contracts as part of a passing 94-test Graph/Bridge/configuration slice. It did not operate a browser. Fixture HTTP tests cannot close keyboard, layout, authentication-dialog, full accessibility or real-model browser acceptance. Keep #53's fixture receipt separate from #11's composed receipt; no new dashboard or renderer change is required.

<!-- lychd-bootstrap-pass3-2026-10-15-53 -->
## Bootstrap browser/toolchain review — 15 October 2026

The bounded browser attempt started the existing synthetic read-only fixture on a verified free loopback port and shut it down cleanly. It registered no runtime capabilities. Available Codex In-app Browser returned `net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT` for status/login and Bridge; server logs showed unauthenticated 401 challenges. No credential was submitted or native login/Bridge–Orb–Loom journey completed; temporary tab/process were closed. This remains a test-surface blocker, not a diagnosed product/browser defect. Do not replace native acceptance with injected auth headers.

**Toolchain blocker closed for the local build profile:** pass 5 prepared official Node **24.20.0** plus npm **12.0.2** under a fresh `/tmp` root, verified Node archive against official SHA-256 and npm archive against registry integrity, and checked exact executable versions. No global runtime change or dependency installation occurred. The same explicit npm wrapper/PATH (including nested npm scripts) passed `make frontend-check` (**341 tests / 23 files**, Svelte 0 errors/0 warnings) and `make frontend-build`. Generated client/assets diff was empty. Source and 49 built-asset fingerprints were retained outside the checkout. The profile used existing `node_modules`, so it does not attest a clean dependency install; the download checks do not claim independent release-signature attestation.

Host/bundled runtimes remain below the manifest floor; use the qualified temporary pair or a separately qualified installation. Native app control is disabled, and the enabled browser inventory still exposes only IAB/MCP Apps despite installed Chrome/Firefox. Next acceptance needs an enabled browser surface that can exercise normal Basic login and credential reuse, followed by synthetic Bridge → same Run in Orb → exact Pattern in Loom → return/refresh. No auth-policy change is justified by this tooling limit.

**Entry point:** #42/#50 supply executable service contracts and multimodal observations. Policy proposals and fixtures can proceed earlier; initial multimodal routing remains deterministic.

## Checklist

- [ ] Admit a versioned selection policy in ADR 22 and typed TOML: weights, units, normalization, defaults, tie-breaks and missing/stale metrics. Compare only candidates satisfying the same semantic demand and hard authority/readiness/resource requirements.
- [ ] Explain eligibility, rejection and score contributions without secrets; retain the current deterministic policy as a compatibility option and prove configuration changes affect newly admitted decisions.
- [ ] Add pool fallback with total deadline/attempt limits and fresh grants; exact selection never substitutes another target. Distinguish proved safe pre-execution retry from submitted/uncertain effects, which require reconciliation.

**Boundary:** Weights cannot override compatibility or authority. Dispatch never starts or evicts a runtime, silently changes language/modality, or admits a remote route merely because local work failed.

**Pinned fallback boundary:** Typed TOML may select a versioned ranking/fallback policy for new admissions, but a Run retains the policy and exact placement truth admitted with its Scroll. Fallback may try only declared, semantically compatible candidates within its admitted road and total deadline. A cold managed candidate yields a handle-free wait, Orchestrator convergence and fresh dispatch; that is not fallback. A submitted or uncertain effect is reconciled under its existing identity. Changing provider, peer, payload, workspace or execution road requires the separately admitted Spellweaver decision tracked by #29/#62, never an implicit next candidate.

Extend the proven chat/Echo/Vision path with measured resource policy and demanding multi-model scenarios.

**Entry point:** #50 supplies the multimodal acceptance and measurements needed for completion. Policy proposals and fixtures can proceed earlier.

## Checklist

- [ ] Stress multiple models within one dynamic Soulstone and competing chat/speech/visual runtimes; verify duplicate-load suppression, per-model readiness and whole-Animator lease drain when loading may evict neighbours.
- [ ] Define and admit a typed TOML resource policy in ADR 23 using measured headroom and load/switch cost, explicit units/defaults and missing-data behaviour; preserve ownership and hard conflict rules.
- [ ] Exercise concurrent requests, priority/FIFO fairness and repeated transitions; measure waiting and switching overhead without silently preempting active work.
- [ ] Add a topology-aware contention fixture: one model spans overlapping devices, disjoint work fits, and an extra demand does not. Include stale observations and an observation/admission race; GPUs are not interchangeable slots. Retain an eight-device stress fixture separately from the named physical profile actually tested.
- [ ] Test cancellation, partial activation and compensation on a named host; record restored, declined or contained outcomes for Graph/Nexus and #36.

**Boundary:** Orchestration makes an already selected capability ready. Candidate-selection weights and fallback belong to #17. Current policy does not measure VRAM or switch cost; those are new work.

**Connections:** Extends #6 and #50; coordinates contracts with #7/#17 without reciprocal completion blockers.

**Later:** Multi-host placement, durable reservations/fencing, preemption and autonomous recovery, scoped from these results.

**References:** [ADR 23](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/23-orchestrator.md) · [ADR 12](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/12-configuration.md).

**Contribution entry:** Contribute a measured runtime scenario or one resource-policy fixture.

## Orchestration review journey

As each instrument slice lands, preserve one linked review route rather than building another dashboard:

| Instrument | What the orchestration review should expose | What it must not claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bridge / Circle (#11) | Intent, canonical Run, pinned Pattern revision, current ledger status, consent/cancellation state, and entry to Orb | Complete scheduler, worker, or physical-runtime truth |
| Loom (#14) | The exact declared Scroll: stations, permitted branches, capability and execution-road demands, and immutable revision | Live traversal, readiness, or proof that a declaration executed |
| Orb (#13 / #36) | Retained Run, station-attempt, delivery, wait, road-decision, transition, `AgentJob`/A2A task and effect evidence, with gaps visible | Authority to retry, cancel, transition hardware, or invent missing events |
| Nexus (#12) | Current declared/observed local capabilities and admitted readiness-transition request, plan, outcome, uncertainty and correlation back to Orb | Queue order, remote-road authority, policy editing, or a guarantee that preview state remains current |
| Atlas (#15) | The continuing concern, decision and explicit references to the exact Bridge conversation or Orb evidence under review | Runtime control or automatic adoption of a review conclusion |

The intended path is Bridge → Orb, then Orb → Loom for declared score and Orb → Nexus for a correlated physical transition; Atlas may retain the concern and citations. Screen-to-screen links remain coordination work, not circular completion blockers. #62 uses this route as the operator-facing review of its advanced synthetic scenario; its existence does not make every advanced field delivered.

- [ ] Keyboard access, visible loading/error/stale states and protected API access.

Provide the CLI foundation to initialize, inspect the setup plan and remove a local test installation.

## Checklist

- [ ] `lychd --help` exposes the command structure with clear errors and exit codes, without requiring a running database or application.
- [ ] `init` creates the Codex, Crypt and Forge layout using XDG paths; effectful init runs as a non-root user.
- [ ] Check the PostgreSQL storage filesystem, Btrfs tools and permissions.
- [ ] For an absent `postgres/data` on supported Btrfs, create a subvolume and verify NOCOW (`+C`) before database writes.
- [ ] Use an ordinary directory where safe if Btrfs preparation is unavailable; log failed NOCOW with the path, reason and next action.
- [ ] Preserve existing storage and permissions; record created resources and make repeated init safe.
- [ ] `del` previews and confirms removal, deletes only verified owned resources, and preserves external storage and shared directories.
- [ ] Block unsafe or uncertain removal; provide an explicit operator handoff for privileged Btrfs cleanup.
- [ ] Both commands support `--dry-run`; tests cover `init → del → init`, Btrfs/fallback and preservation of pre-existing resources.

**Starting point:** [CLI](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/src/lychd/__main__.py), [layout tests](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/tests/unit/system/services/test_layout.py); [delivery boundary](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/state-of-the-work.md#core-cli-rites).
